contract.sync_assumed: none beyond warp convergence of the logical warp's lanes
contract.type_constraints: bf16 keys packed into one 32-bit word (key bits high, inverted 16-bit index low, N at most 65536), fp32 keys packed into one 64-bit word (key bits high, inverted 32-bit index low), int32 source indices derived from the striped position
contract.nan_behavior: a NaN key orders by its sign bit (positive NaN above every finite key, negative NaN below), deterministic, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is mapped to +0.0 before packing so the two zeros compare equal
contract.tie_break_support: inherent in the word order: among equal keys the smaller index gives the larger word, prefer_smaller_index costs nothing (psi cells equal the ng cells to the cycle, same code)
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: the first k striped positions are sorted by (key descending, index ascending)
contract.k_range: [1, MaxK] with MaxK = round_up(k, 32) <= N at compile time, k 4 to 16 pay the k 32 network
contract.n_range: N = 32 x IPT, IPT >= 1, measured 32, 64 and 128 (bf16 N at most 65536)

correctness.notes: Oracle battery (random seeds, tie_heavy, sorted_asc, sorted_desc, pivot_tie, all_equal, signed_zero, inf_denorm, quantized_random, relu_quantized) passed in every cell for both requirements, including the exact prefer_smaller_index check with signed zeros. The prefer_smaller_index cells have an A/A control (W1_reference does not support the requirement) measured in a second lock section of the same lease right after the not_guaranteed section, see the batch files. Two W1 optimizer instances shared one agent id on 2026-10-25. This card is Instance A (opt-W1, worktree cccl-topk-swarm-W1, branch exp/topk-swarm/W1): W1_packed, W1_level, the sub-warp adapters and the N2 verdict from W1_level against W1_packed. Instance B (opt-W1b) owns the same-code eager against level comparison and the fp32 native min max pairs variant, report approaches/W1/REPORT_W1b.md. Built on the node against the shared harness at swarm commit b6bfae9a37bb, adapter sources at W1 worktree commit ccc1166d9c.

low_level: Instruction mix per network from the SASS of the latency kernel (two inlined copies per kernel, counts per copy): bf16 u32 index-in-key at N 32 is 15 SHFL, 19 ISETP, 17 SEL, 20 LOP3, 10 PLOP3 against the pairs reference's 30 SHFL, 14 ISETP, 31 SEL, 41 LOP3, 20 PLOP3, 6 PRMT: one shuffle per stage instead of two and no bf16 pack and unpack. ptxas does not turn CUB's bool comparator into VIMNMX for the u32 words: the exchange stays ISETP, ISETP, PLOP3, SEL (2 VIMNMX in the whole kernel), so the observation of issue #12160 that integral keys already get IMNMX does not hold for the WarpBitonicSortNetwork merge_stage form with its two compares and the reverse test.

fp32 as a u64 word: 2 SHFL per stage like the pairs reference (the CUDA 13.4 header splits the 64-bit shuffle into two 32-bit ones, no asm), the compare is a dependent ISETP plus ISETP.EX pair per direction (4 ISETP and 2 SEL per stage, 34 ISETP and 31 SEL per network at N 32) against the reference's 2 FSETP, 1 FSEL, 1 SEL. Registers 24 at N 32, 32 at N 64, 41 to 42 at N 128 against the reference's 22, 26 and 32 to 33. No spills, no stack frame, 0 BAR.SYNC, no shared memory beyond the harness output buffer. BRA count equals the no-op kernel's (5), no branch inside the network (T20 check).

bf16 registers 20 at N 32, 23 at N 64, 27 at N 128 against 26 and 36 for the reference, occupancy 8 blocks of 256 threads per SM in every throughput cell for both. The packing (canonicalize -0.0, sign flip, shift, or with the inverted index) is about 7 instructions per item, independent across items, and is inside the measured number.

The generate-only control slope is 48 cycles for every warp cell, R squared 1.0000 on every fit, canaries 32.001 cycles per shuffle op at start and end of each section, throughput canary 3609 to 3611 us.
algorithmic: bf16: the index in the key word turns the pairs network into a keys-only network with one 32-bit shuffle per stage: 1.24x at N 32 (626 against 778 cycles), 1.03x at N 64 for k 4 to 16 (1150 against 1187) and 1.29x at k 32 (905 against 1164), 1.54x to 1.66x at N 128 (1367 against 2267 at k 4 to 16, 1521 against 2340 at k 32, 1598 against 2562 at k 64). Throughput 1.81x at N 32 (244 against 135 Gelem/s), 2.24x at N 64 (271 against 121), 2.31x at N 128 (264 against 114) and 2.45x at N 128 k 64 (233 against 95). The gain grows with N because the reference shuffles the 16-bit keys and the 32-bit indices separately and converts per stage.

prefer_smaller_index is free: the psi cells equal the not_guaranteed cells to the cycle (bf16 626, 1150, 905, 1367, 1521, 1598, fp32 597, 990, 2408, 2583) because the same code runs and the word order carries the tie-break. This is the first warp primitive in the study with the exact requirement at zero cost.

fp32 in a 64-bit word costs 15 to 19 percent against the pairs reference at N 64 and 128 (990 against 846, 2408 against 2038, 2583 against 2255 cycles, throughput 166 against 204, 156 against 192, 136 against 165 Gelem/s) and ties at N 32 (597 against 605, 201 against 204 Gelem/s). That is the price of the exact tie-break for fp32 in the eager structure, there is no 32-bit word for a 32-bit key plus index.

MaxK rounds k up to 32, so k 4, 8 and 16 share one number per N as in the reference. The eager loop's cost per added 32-item tile is 740 cycles for bf16 (1150 at N 64 to 1367 at N 128 is less because the control's N 64 k 16 cell is the anomalous one, see surprises) and 710 for fp32 (990 to 2408 for two added tiles).
negative: The u64 word is not the way to carry fp32 with prefer_smaller_index when latency matters at N at least 64: 0.85x against the pairs reference. The comparison to make is a pairs network with a (key, index) comparator or the native min max pairs form (Instance B's slice).
At fp32 N 32 the packing gives nothing over pairs (597 against 605 cycles, 201 against 204 Gelem/s).
surprises: The CUB eager latency depends on k at fixed MaxK and identical network: bf16 N 64 is 1150 cycles for k 4 to 16 and 905 for k 32, N 128 is 1367 for k 4 to 16 and 1521 for k 32, fp32 N 64 and 128 do not move. Only the output store count differs (456 against 440 SASS instructions in the latency kernel at N 64). Throughput is identical (271 against 272 Gelem/s). The same effect appears in the level network at sub-warp LW 16 N 128 fp32 (2320 for k 8, 3431 for k 16). It looks like a ptxas schedule effect on the latency chain and is not understood.

ptxas does not emit min max for the u32 bool comparator network, so the integer word alone does not buy the 2-instruction exchange of issue #12160, the exchange has to be written as keep_max ? max : min (the W1_level network does and gets two predicated VIMNMX per stage).
open_questions: Why does the latency chain of one network shift by up to 25 percent with the number of output stores, in both directions? A SASS diff of the N 64 k 16 against k 32 kernels or a harness option that stores all MaxK outputs would separate a chain artifact from a real schedule effect.
Does the halved SASS count of the bf16 path carry into the batched segmented kernels, where both forms already reach 8 blocks per SM?

Would a min max operator path in WarpBitonicSort (issue #12160) give the eager CUB code the VIMNMX exchange for integer words without a custom network? The W1_level numbers bound the gain at two tiles (bf16 N 64 k 32: 905 to 695 cycles, which also contains the restructuring).
